source_title: Finalized authoritative structured areas are mutable, unsigned and outside correction lineage
original_evidence: Migration 0128 defines `session_block_areas` as the authoritative ordered area/laterality rows and explicitly grants authenticated studio members SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE under an `FOR ALL` membership policy. The finalization trigger list predates this table and does not guard it. The signed snapshot does not include it, and the correction dispatcher has no structured-area target.
original_acceptance_criteria: Fresh-DB test: finalize a record, then assert direct insert/update/delete and area-replacement RPC all fail; assert a reasoned correction creates immutable before/after versions; assert snapshot hash changes when area/laterality/order changes.
original_recommended_fix: Emergency containment migration: attach a finalized-parent guard to `session_block_areas`; revoke direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE from `authenticated`; permit mutations only through a validated draft-only command. Add structured areas to canonical snapshot v2 and correction/amendment support. Run a production-safe audit query for post-finalization area mutations before enabling or expanding use.
original_launch_gate: Forward-only migration. First contain writes, then introduce snapshot v2/correction support. Do not rewrite historical signed snapshots silently; version the snapshot schema and record any remediation as an attributed correction.

source_title: Finalization can race a child write and sign a state different from the committed finalized rows
original_evidence: Child-table write guards perform a plain parent-status SELECT. The finalizer locks only the session row, builds the snapshot, hashes it and inserts finalization artifacts. It does not lock every child row/table or force child mutations through a lock-compatible command.
original_acceptance_criteria: DB integration test with two independent transactions and barriers: child mutation pauses after authorization, finalizer completes, child commit must block then fail; repeat for each child table and structured areas.
original_recommended_fix: Use a single per-session advisory/row-lock protocol for every clinical mutation and finalization. Commands that mutate children should lock the parent `FOR UPDATE` before checking draft status; finalization should acquire the same lock before collecting the snapshot.
original_launch_gate: Ship after the P0 guard or in the same containment series. Keep finalization disabled until the concurrency test passes from a fresh DB.

source_title: The signed finalization snapshot omits authoritative clinical fields added after the original design
original_evidence: The snapshot builder serializes a subset of session/block/entry/image fields. It does not include the authoritative `session_block_areas` rows and does not cover later probe-inventory linkage and conditional numbing fields introduced by migrations 0155/0156. A successful hash therefore is not a complete representation of the record visible to a practitioner.
original_acceptance_criteria: Golden DB tests create records differing one clinically meaningful field at a time and assert canonical snapshot/hash differences; verify round-trip rendering and export from the snapshot.
original_recommended_fix: Introduce a versioned canonical snapshot schema that includes every clinically authoritative table/field, sorted deterministically. Define explicit inclusion/exclusion rules and fail finalization if an unknown required schema version is encountered.
original_launch_gate: Do not mutate old snapshots. Store `snapshot_schema_version`; preserve legacy version verification and use attributed corrections/backfill attestations where needed.

source_title: Intake submission can overwrite a concurrent practitioner edit to the client profile
original_evidence: Submission uses a status compare-and-set for the intake, then separately reads the client, builds a patch from intake answers and updates the client by `id`. There is no version predicate, `updated_at` compare, field-level merge contract or transaction spanning submit and profile synchronization.
original_acceptance_criteria: Two-connection DB test: update client after intake read but before sync; command must preserve the newer value or return a conflict requiring review.
original_recommended_fix: Move synchronization into a database command with explicit field authority and optimistic concurrency. Prefer storing intake answers as immutable submitted evidence and requiring a deliberate practitioner-reviewed merge for fields that can conflict.
original_launch_gate: Avoid silently re-running historical intake sync. Add a visible “profile differs from submitted intake” reconciliation state.

source_title: A draft intake can be marked reviewed without ever being submitted
original_evidence: The review action updates the intake to `reviewed` using intake ID and studio scope. It does not require current status `submitted`, verify that the intake belongs to the route client, check one affected row, or capture a submitted version as the reviewed artifact.
original_acceptance_criteria: DB tests for draft→reviewed rejection, wrong-client rejection, duplicate review idempotency and concurrent submit/review ordering.
original_recommended_fix: Implement a database transition command requiring `status = submitted`, matching `client_id`, active practitioner attribution, submitted version/hash and exactly one affected row. Make invalid transitions fail closed.
original_launch_gate: Existing erroneously reviewed rows require a safe audit/reconciliation report, not silent downgrade.

source_title: The owner export is described as complete but omits material clinical, privacy, payment and media records
original_evidence: The export reads a selected set of CSV datasets and explicitly excludes image binaries/storage paths and payment tables. It also omits intake/health forms, consent signatures/templates, clinical snapshots/corrections/amendments, portal messages and several audit/provenance tables. The UI says data is exportable and the README/action copy describes broad completeness.
original_acceptance_criteria: Seed one row/object in every exportable table/bucket; export, validate manifest/checksums and import into a verification tool. Test large studios and revoked/deleted records under retention policy.
original_recommended_fix: Define a versioned export manifest covering every tenant-owned table, consent/intake versions, snapshots/corrections, payment metadata, communication/audit records and image binaries with checksums. Generate a completeness report and allow independent validation.
original_launch_gate: Correct the UI immediately to say “partial export” until complete. Do not perform destructive offboarding based on the current artifact.

source_title: Quick Import is non-transactional and can strand clients without their treatment history
original_evidence: The action bulk-inserts clients, then inserts treatment-memory rows. If memory insertion fails, the clients remain while the batch is marked voided. A retry skips existing clients, so the original file may not repair the missing history. The final completed-state update result is also not checked.
original_acceptance_criteria: Fault-injection DB tests at every phase; retry same batch must converge to one correct result; cross-tenant IDs and spreadsheet formula payloads must fail safely.
original_recommended_fix: Implement a transactional import RPC or staged tables with validate→preview→commit. Give every source row stable identity, upsert idempotently, persist rejected rows and support safe resume/rollback.
original_launch_gate: Until fixed, require verified backups and post-import reconciliation; label workflow operator-assisted and do not use it as a self-serve launch dependency.

source_title: Any authenticated practitioner can choose an arbitrary session charge amount up to CAD 2,000
original_evidence: The action comments state the session price is a suggestion, accepts `amount_dollars` from the practitioner form, and permits any authenticated practitioner in the studio to initiate the charge. Stripe account, customer and payment method are server-derived, but amount authority is not owner-only or tied to an immutable invoice/service/session calculation.
original_acceptance_criteria: Action/DB/E2E tests reject member-supplied arbitrary values, altered hidden fields, wrong session/client/account and excessive deviations; verify receipts use the final authorized amount.
original_recommended_fix: Derive the default amount from server-authoritative services/session charges. Permit adjustments only to owners or an explicit role, with bounded reason codes, confirmation and audit. Consider dual confirmation above a threshold.
original_launch_gate: Before enabling another studio, reconcile existing charge attempts against expected service/session amounts and document the approved pricing authority.

source_title: Sentry can receive bearer credentials embedded in URL path segments
original_evidence: Request and breadcrumb scrubbing removes query strings but preserves path segments. Hone places high-entropy bearer credentials in the path. The generic regexes target emails, JWTs, Bearer headers and selected token-like formats; an opaque random path segment can survive. Error events or sampled traces can therefore transmit it to Sentry.
original_acceptance_criteria: Sentry scrub tests with realistic opaque tokens in request URL, transaction, span description, breadcrumb and exception context; assert the token never appears in serialized event JSON.
original_recommended_fix: Canonicalize sensitive routes to templates before Sentry processing, e.g. `/intake/[token]`; drop transaction names/URLs/breadcrumb data for all bearer routes; add server-side allowlisted route metadata instead. Rotate/revoke credentials after suspected leakage.
original_launch_gate: Deploy scrub before enabling tracing broadly. Review Sentry retention/access and search historical events for route patterns without exporting raw tokens.

source_title: Availability, overrides, blockouts and service scheduling settings remain directly writable by any studio member
original_evidence: Early RLS grants full membership-scoped DML to schedule configuration tables. Later atomic/locked owner actions improve the intended path but do not remove the direct table capability.
original_acceptance_criteria: DB tests assert members cannot modify another practitioner/studio-wide settings; approved commands serialize with public/internal booking.
original_recommended_fix: Revoke broad DML; separate owner-managed studio policy, practitioner self-availability and system materialization commands. Each command should lock the same capacity authority used by booking.
original_launch_gate: Coordinate with public-booking command migration so there is one consistent lock protocol.

source_title: Public booking ignores the practitioner-capacity emergency booking kill switch
original_evidence: Internal booking V2 locks the studio/capacity state and checks the booking-enabled control. Public booking inserts directly through the admin client after a slot recheck and never calls the authoritative command or the kill-switch check.
original_acceptance_criteria: DB/browser test toggles the kill switch between slot display and submit; submission must fail with a safe unavailable message and create no client/appointment side effects.
original_recommended_fix: Route all public appointment creation through a public-safe authoritative DB command that checks global/studio/practitioner gates under the capacity lock immediately before insert.
original_launch_gate: Ship before relying on the kill switch operationally or enabling multi-practitioner public booking.

source_title: Public booking is outside the capacity lock and can race schedule edits or authoritative internal commands
original_evidence: Public booking performs a slot recheck in application code and later inserts directly. It does not acquire the same studio/practitioner capacity lock used by internal booking and schedule writers, so the check and insert are not serialized with an availability change.
original_acceptance_criteria: Two-connection tests for public booking versus override, blockout, service archive, practitioner deactivation, internal booking and kill-switch toggle.
original_recommended_fix: Move public booking into the same DB transaction/lock protocol as internal creation; derive service duration and practitioner eligibility under lock; atomically create client/consent/appointment/audit or return no side effects.
original_launch_gate: Requires a compatibility wrapper for the anonymous/token surface; do not expose a broadly executable unsafe RPC.

source_title: DST conversion silently shifts nonexistent local times and cannot represent the second repeated hour
original_evidence: The helper explicitly documents that a Toronto spring-forward local time such as 02:30 maps one hour before the requested wall time, and a fall-back repeated 01:xx resolves to the first occurrence. Booking/move actions do not round-trip validate the selected wall time or expose an occurrence choice.
original_acceptance_criteria: Unit and browser tests for Toronto/New York spring-forward and fall-back, midnight boundaries, long services and Google/notification rendering.
original_recommended_fix: Use a timezone library/API that detects nonexistent and ambiguous wall times. Reject gaps with a clear UI message. For overlaps, require/derive an explicit offset/occurrence and round-trip validate before writing.
original_launch_gate: Data audit for appointments created in transition windows; do not automatically shift historical rows without practitioner review.

source_title: A same-studio member can re-parent a draft clinical session to the wrong client through direct DML
original_evidence: Session and block policies are membership-scoped. The identity-freeze trigger protects selected session identity fields only after finalization. While draft, an authenticated studio member can update `client_id` directly if the row remains in the same studio.
original_acceptance_criteria: DB tests reject direct client/studio/practitioner re-parenting in draft and finalized states; test approved command only under owner/authorized role with audit event.
original_recommended_fix: Freeze session identity from creation except through a dedicated audited reassignment command with strict no-child or explicit migration semantics. Revoke direct UPDATE on identity columns from authenticated users.
original_launch_gate: Audit existing sessions for identity changes where history permits. Avoid a blanket rewrite of affected records.

source_title: Broad authenticated appointment DML bypasses owner/member command authorization, invariants and audit
original_evidence: The appointment table is exposed under broad studio-membership DML while newer create/move commands implement role checks, capacity locks, authoritative duration and availability validation. A caller can bypass the newer command by calling PostgREST directly.
original_acceptance_criteria: Direct DML negative tests for every restricted field/status transition; command tests assert locks, authority, audit and one-row effects.
original_recommended_fix: Revoke authenticated INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on appointments; expose narrow SECURITY DEFINER commands for create, move, cancel, complete, no-show and approved administrative repair. Use column privileges as an intermediate containment step.
original_launch_gate: Stage behind feature flags only if legacy clients require migration; instrument denied direct writes and provide an operator repair command.

source_title: SaaS subscription billing and entitlements are absent
original_evidence: Stripe Connect client payments are distinct from billing studios for Hone. There is no demonstrated plan subscription, dunning, entitlement, trial, cancellation, invoice/tax or access-suspension control plane.
original_acceptance_criteria: Fake-provider subscription lifecycle tests including duplicate/out-of-order webhooks, dunning, plan changes and cancellation.
original_recommended_fix: After the safety pilot, build separate platform-billing customer/subscription/entitlement models with webhook idempotency, grace periods, manual override audit and no coupling to clinical data deletion.
original_launch_gate: Defer until studio #2 safety; required before scaling paid acquisition.

source_title: Calendar-feed bearer URLs lack rotation/revocation UI and last-used telemetry
original_evidence: The feed uses a high-entropy bearer URL, hash-only storage and generic busy content—good privacy foundations. The route comments defer a user-facing rotate/revoke capability, and no clear last-used telemetry is exposed.
original_acceptance_criteria: Browser/route tests verify old token revocation, new token activation and no raw token in telemetry/Sentry.
original_recommended_fix: Add owner-controlled rotate/revoke, overlapping cutover window, last-used timestamp/client fingerprint minimization and alerts for unusual use.
original_launch_gate: Coordinate with F-PRIV-001 before broader feed use.

source_title: Hosting, encryption and compliance-facing UI claims are not fully supported by evidence in the ZIP
original_evidence: One settings surface says data is hosted in Canada and encrypted at rest, while the privacy page says Supabase infrastructure is in the United States and Canadian residency is being evaluated. The ZIP cannot prove cloud region, backup encryption, processor contracts or current deployment topology.
original_acceptance_criteria: Release gate checks a versioned claims manifest against environment/contract evidence; manual legal approval recorded.
original_recommended_fix: Reconcile every public/in-app claim to a signed infrastructure and subprocessor register. Use precise wording: operated from Canada is not the same as data residency in Canada. Obtain qualified privacy/legal review.
original_launch_gate: Correct contradictory text before additional sales; do not claim compliance broadly.

source_title: Whole-session-copy provenance can disappear through cascading deletes
original_evidence: The provenance ledger references source and target with `ON DELETE CASCADE`. Deleting either record can erase evidence that settings were copied, weakening historical attribution even though the copy itself is carefully designed.
original_acceptance_criteria: DB test deletes/archives source/target and verifies provenance remains interpretable.
original_recommended_fix: Use durable tombstone identifiers or `ON DELETE RESTRICT/SET NULL` with immutable source fingerprint and human-readable provenance retained according to policy.
original_launch_gate: Coordinate with retention/legal-hold design.

source_title: Critical local verification lanes were environment-blocked
original_evidence: Dependencies could not be installed; the local shell is outside one locked dependency’s declared engine range; no local Supabase/browser stack was available. Typecheck, lint, build, unit, DB, browser, payment and Google lanes were not executed.
original_acceptance_criteria: Exact-head CI artifact with all lane results and fresh-DB migration application.
original_recommended_fix: Run the exact archive/commit in hermetic Node 20.20+ CI with locked registry cache, local Supabase, Playwright and fake providers. Publish immutable logs and checksums.
original_launch_gate: This is a mandatory launch gate, not a request to weaken or edit tests.

source_title: Google Calendar “not registered” documentation is contradicted by Vercel cron configuration
original_evidence: `vercel.json` registers `/api/cron/calendar-reconcile` and `/api/cron/calendar-sync` on daily schedules. Some comments/docs describe those routes as not registered. The database claim path still appears to fail closed when `worker_enabled=false`, so registration alone does not prove provider calls.
original_acceptance_criteria: Config test enumerates registered cron routes and verifies each route’s fail-closed auth/global/studio/no-work behaviour.
original_recommended_fix: Make deploy configuration the source of truth, update docs, expose a runtime dormancy dashboard and require dual global+studio gates plus zero-work metrics.
original_launch_gate: No Google enablement until deploy config, flags, secrets and operator checklist reconcile.

source_title: Google refresh-token key rotation has no dual-key window and requires reconnect on key change
original_evidence: Ciphertext is versioned and AES-GCM fail-closed, which is good. The runtime exposes only the active key; a version mismatch makes the connection reconnect-required rather than decrypting with a previous key and rewrapping.
original_acceptance_criteria: Rotation test with mixed key versions, concurrent refresh and rollback; no plaintext logging.
original_recommended_fix: Support current+previous key IDs or KMS envelope encryption, rewrap secrets under controlled jobs, monitor completion and retire old keys after verification.
original_launch_gate: Design before broad Google rollout; current reconnect posture may be acceptable for a tiny controlled pilot if documented.

source_title: Inbound busy-time import and true two-way Google Calendar synchronization are not built
original_evidence: The archive supports connection and outbound-sync foundations. It does not establish inbound busy-time ingestion or conflict-aware two-way synchronization. Marketing/roadmap language must preserve that distinction.
original_acceptance_criteria: Future provider-contract tests for recurrence, timezone, deletion, rate limits and conflict reconciliation.
original_recommended_fix: Keep scope labeled outbound-only. Validate whether inbound busy import is truly required; if built, define source of truth, privacy, recurrence, deletion and conflict policy first.
original_launch_gate: Defer until outbound reliability and real demand are proven.

source_title: No complete offboarding, studio deletion and provider-disconnection workflow exists
original_evidence: The archive lacks one controlled workflow that freezes writes, creates/verifies a complete export, handles retention/legal hold, revokes tokens, disconnects Google/Stripe, resolves storage, schedules deletion and records approvals.
original_acceptance_criteria: End-to-end sandbox offboarding test including retry/rollback and post-delete access denial.
original_recommended_fix: Design a state machine with owner/admin approvals, export checksum, retention clock, provider revocation, legal hold, deletion jobs and final certificate.
original_launch_gate: Required before contractual self-serve cancellation or 10 studios.

source_title: Studio provisioning creates only the studio and owner invitation; onboarding remains operator-assisted
original_evidence: The action performs two core service-role writes and compensates if the invitation fails. It does not provision a complete service catalogue, availability, intake/consent defaults, policies, provider state, payment fee controls, practitioners or launch verification.
original_acceptance_criteria: Provision from empty state twice, interrupt each step and verify resume/rollback; produce launch manifest.
original_recommended_fix: Create a versioned provisioning template and idempotent launch workflow with defaults, explicit choices, validation, recovery and evidence. Avoid hidden production SQL.
original_launch_gate: Founder-led assistance is acceptable to 10 studios, but the process must be repeatable and auditable.

source_title: Onboarding declares readiness after only service, availability and public-booking checks
original_evidence: Only three steps are required for `requiredComplete`; payments are optional and many safety/operational prerequisites are absent: privacy terms, consent/intake review, practitioner roles, export test, reminders, incident contact, provider flags, training and launch verification.
original_acceptance_criteria: Onboarding tests ensure no studio reaches launched state with any mandatory gate missing; operator override requires reason/audit/expiry.
original_recommended_fix: Separate “booking configured” from “production launch approved.” Add a versioned launch gate with mandatory safety, data, provider, training and support evidence.
original_launch_gate: Use manual approval for 0–10 studios; automate only after the checklist is proven.

source_title: Public rate limiting intentionally fails open during limiter/provider failure
original_evidence: The contract explicitly allows public slot, booking and token-route requests when the limiter backend errors. This prioritizes availability but removes abuse containment precisely during provider/configuration failure.
original_acceptance_criteria: Fault-injection load tests with limiter unavailable; ensure mutation throughput remains bounded and legitimate read traffic has a controlled degraded path.
original_recommended_fix: Use endpoint-specific posture: local bounded fallback, stricter fail-closed/degraded mode for mutation/token verification, circuit breakers and per-studio/IP/device signals. Return privacy-safe errors.
original_launch_gate: Coordinate with public booking atomicity and abuse monitoring.

source_title: Twilio STOP handling scans every phone-bearing client across studios in one service-role process
original_evidence: Twilio signature verification is strong. After verification, the route uses service role to fetch phone-bearing clients broadly, normalizes/filter matches in application memory, then applies a deliberate global phone-wide opt-out across studios.
original_acceptance_criteria: DB tests for multiple studios/shared numbers, indexed query plan and no PII returned to route beyond affected IDs/counts.
original_recommended_fix: Store normalized phone hashes/indexes and execute a narrow audited DB command. Preserve legally required global opt-out semantics only after privacy/legal confirmation, with minimal returned data and explicit provenance.
original_launch_gate: Migrate normalized hashes before volume grows; document consent semantics.

source_title: Appointment reminders depend on an external scheduler with no Vercel cron registration in the archive
original_evidence: The reminder route exists but `vercel.json` registers recurring breaks and Google jobs, not appointment reminders. Documentation may rely on an external scheduler, but the ZIP cannot prove it exists, is authenticated, runs at the required cadence or has heartbeat monitoring.
original_acceptance_criteria: Staging job test plus production no-op heartbeat verification; simulate missed schedule and recovery without duplicates.
original_recommended_fix: Make scheduler ownership explicit, register it in deploy-as-code or an independently attested provider, add heartbeat/lag metrics and alert on missed windows.
original_launch_gate: Mandatory launch evidence for each studio using reminders.

source_title: No backup restore drill, RPO/RTO, on-call or incident-command evidence is included
original_evidence: The ZIP contains alerts/runbook material but no immutable evidence of backup configuration, restore success, recovery point/objective, incident ownership, escalation or rollback rehearsal.
original_acceptance_criteria: Restore a sanitized environment from backup, verify tenant/data/object counts and run core workflows; record signed results.
original_recommended_fix: Define RPO/RTO, backup scope including storage, quarterly restore drills, incident roles, communication templates, kill switches and deployment rollback evidence.
original_launch_gate: Mandatory before 10 studios and repeated before 50/100.

source_title: Operational alerts have no durable retry and can be lost on database/email failure
original_evidence: The helper redacts and attempts logging, DB insertion and critical email, but deliberately does not throw. A failed alert insert/send is logged and dropped without an outbox or retry.
original_acceptance_criteria: Fault-injection tests for DB, email and logging failures; at least one independent signal must remain observable.
original_recommended_fix: Use a durable local/outbox path where possible, provider-independent fallback metrics and heartbeat monitoring. Track delivery state/retries without exposing PII.
original_launch_gate: Avoid recursive alert storms; define bounded retry/dead-letter behaviour.

source_title: Public booking deposits, card collection, packages and partial payments are not built or deliberately held
original_evidence: The public booking flow does not collect a card/deposit. Packages, split/partial payments and a complete fee lifecycle are absent or held. This is safer than prematurely enabling them, but limits commercial parity.
original_acceptance_criteria: Future provider-contract/E2E tests with amount, consent, cancellation and refund invariants.
original_recommended_fix: Do not build until public booking authority, consent and amount logic are safe. Validate demand and legal/card-authorization wording before implementation.
original_launch_gate: Explicitly defer during P0/P1 remediation.

source_title: Public-booking audit duplicates raw email and free-text notes
original_evidence: The booking audit payload stores raw email and notes in addition to the canonical client/appointment records. Free text may contain sensitive details and duplicates expand access, retention and breach scope.
original_acceptance_criteria: Tests assert raw email, phone and arbitrary notes never appear in audit/log/ops payloads.
original_recommended_fix: Store stable IDs, normalized event metadata and a redacted/hash representation; keep sensitive content only in its canonical protected record. Define audit retention separately.
original_launch_gate: Migrate or redact historical audit payloads only under an approved retention plan.

source_title: Repository provenance is incomplete because the ZIP contains no Git metadata
original_evidence: The archive comment contains a SHA-like value, but branch, commit ancestry, dirty/untracked state, submodules and whether the tree exactly equals that commit cannot be established.
original_acceptance_criteria: CI attestation compares archive tree hash to checked-out commit and records artifact digest.
original_recommended_fix: Future audits should use an immutable Git archive generated by CI with commit, tree hash, lockfile hash, migration manifest, build provenance and deployment ID.
original_launch_gate: Treat every deployment/merge claim in this report as unverified until reconciled.

source_title: Public booking is non-transactional and can leave client/consent side effects when appointment creation fails
original_evidence: Client creation or consent updates occur before the direct appointment insert. Appointment collision/failure can return an error after those earlier mutations have committed. Marketing consent and audit/provider side effects occur in later stages as well.
original_acceptance_criteria: Fault-injection and race tests assert zero durable side effects on every rejected submit.
original_recommended_fix: Create a single public-booking DB command that validates and atomically creates/reuses client, records consent evidence, inserts appointment and audit row. Dispatch email/SMS from an outbox after commit.
original_launch_gate: Provide a cleanup/reconciliation report for orphan clients created by failed booking attempts.

source_title: Knowing an existing client email permits nuisance bookings against that client record
original_evidence: The existing-client branch normalizes email and reuses a matching client without authenticating control of the address. This is common in low-friction booking, but it permits impersonation/nuisance bookings and can mutate selected consent fields.
original_acceptance_criteria: Browser tests for known-email impersonation, repeated nuisance submissions, rate-limiter outage and confirmation expiry.
original_recommended_fix: Choose an explicit risk posture: email verification/magic link for recognized clients, confirmation before high-impact bookings, anti-abuse scoring and non-mutating consent handling. Preserve accessible first-time booking.
original_launch_gate: Validate with studio workflow; classify as accepted limitation only with controls and disclosure.

source_title: Retention, deletion, legal hold and complete studio purge are not implemented as a coherent process
original_evidence: Policies discuss retention, but code evidence does not show a complete schedule that applies consistently to database rows, audit logs, snapshots, storage objects, provider data, backups and legal holds.
original_acceptance_criteria: Sandbox lifecycle test across DB, storage, providers and export; backup deletion limitations explicitly documented.
original_recommended_fix: Create a data inventory with purpose, legal basis, retention, deletion/anonymization and hold rules; implement idempotent jobs and evidence reports with qualified legal/privacy review.
original_launch_gate: Required before self-serve deletion and broader regulated-jurisdiction sales.

source_title: Studio export is unbounded, built fully in memory and duplicated as base64
original_evidence: The action loads all selected rows, creates the entire ZIP in server memory and converts it to base64 for return through a server action. Binary expansion and duplicate buffers increase memory significantly.
original_acceptance_criteria: Load test at projected 100k clients/1m records and large image corpus; enforce quotas and cancellation.
original_recommended_fix: Generate exports asynchronously with paginated/streamed reads, object storage, manifest/checksums, expiry and resumable status. Stream download rather than base64 server-action payload.
original_launch_gate: Pair with complete-export redesign rather than optimizing the incomplete format.

source_title: “Next available” scans dates sequentially and can multiply database work per request
original_evidence: The action loops day by day up to its horizon and invokes slot generation repeatedly. Each day can issue several DB reads. Sparse calendars and public abuse can multiply latency and load.
original_acceptance_criteria: Benchmark sparse/dense calendars at 10/50/100 studios and assert maximum query/time budget.
original_recommended_fix: Query/materialize candidate availability in bounded ranges, cache safe schedule inputs, paginate search and enforce a request work budget with metrics.
original_launch_gate: Address before paid traffic; do not optimize ahead of correctness/atomicity.

source_title: Public multi-practitioner booking is not implemented safely; appointments resolve to owner or null
original_evidence: The public action looks up the studio owner and assigns that practitioner (or null). It does not expose a validated practitioner choice, no-preference allocation or capacity-aware assignment.
original_acceptance_criteria: Browser/DB tests for chosen practitioner, no preference, parallel practitioners, deactivation, reassignment and cross-studio practitioner substitution.
original_recommended_fix: Add explicit service-practitioner eligibility, practitioner choice/no-preference policy and atomic assignment under the capacity lock. Do not infer readiness from schema alone.
original_launch_gate: Keep public multi-practitioner disabled until a controlled pilot passes.

source_title: Slot generation ignores several database query errors and can return misleading availability
original_evidence: Blockout, capacity/default and reservation queries consume `.data` without consistently surfacing `.error`. A failed query can be interpreted as no blockouts/reservations or missing defaults rather than an unavailable scheduling service.
original_acceptance_criteria: Unit tests inject each query error; public submit must revalidate and create no booking; UI distinguishes “no availability” from system failure.
original_recommended_fix: Fail closed for mutation-relevant availability, return a distinct temporary-unavailable state, emit redacted ops metrics and avoid caching incomplete results.
original_launch_gate: Ship with public atomic command; do not expose provider/database details.

source_title: No staging, canary rollout or migration-rehearsal evidence is included
original_evidence: The repository has local test intent and production gate scripts, but the ZIP cannot establish a production-like staging environment, canary process, migration rehearsal against realistic data or rollback evidence.
original_acceptance_criteria: Rehearse P0 snapshot migration and public-booking command on representative data before production.
original_recommended_fix: Create sanitized production-shape staging, migration dry-run/rehearsal, feature-flag canary by studio, automated smoke tests and rollback/forward-fix decision records.
original_launch_gate: Required before 10–50 studio growth.

source_title: Treatment-image upload can leave orphaned private objects when metadata insertion and cleanup both fail
original_evidence: The action uploads the object first, then inserts metadata. On metadata failure it attempts deletion and emits an alert if cleanup fails. There is no durable reconciliation queue or periodic orphan scanner shown.
original_acceptance_criteria: Fault-injection tests for every failure point and reconciler convergence without cross-tenant deletion.
original_recommended_fix: Create a durable upload intent/object ledger and reconciler; use deterministic state transitions, checksums and retention-safe quarantine. Periodically compare bucket objects to metadata.
original_launch_gate: Do not expose orphan paths; preserve incident/audit evidence.

source_title: A large source-string assertion surface creates false confidence about runtime behaviour
original_evidence: Source/migration shape tests are useful guardrails, but many assert that strings, comments, function names or fragments exist. They cannot prove RLS under real roles, transaction isolation, provider request semantics or UI behaviour.
original_acceptance_criteria: Coverage map must identify the behavioural layer for every P0/P1 regression and fail releases that have source-only coverage.
original_recommended_fix: Label test classes in CI; shift highest-risk assertions to DB/browser/concurrency/provider-contract behaviour; retain source guards only for truly static invariants.
original_launch_gate: Incremental conversion; do not delete guards until stronger tests exist.

source_title: Critical concurrency regressions are missing for finalizer-vs-child-write and public-booking-vs-schedule mutation
original_evidence: The suite covers selected duplicate/finalizer cases and hard-overlap scenarios, but the two confirmed races do not have two-connection barrier tests that reproduce their transaction ordering.
original_acceptance_criteria: The regression itself is the required evidence: old code must fail, fixed code must pass reliably across repeated runs.
original_recommended_fix: Add deterministic two-connection DB tests with synchronization barriers and repeat under relevant isolation levels. Test every entry point against the same lock authority.
original_launch_gate: Run in mandatory DB CI, not an optional slow lane.

source_title: Mobile Chromium coverage is not physical iOS Safari or accessibility acceptance evidence
original_evidence: The repository has a mobile browser lane, but emulated/Chromium behaviour cannot prove WebKit/Safari quirks, physical keyboard/viewport behaviour, camera/photo flows, screen-reader semantics or practitioner usability on real devices.
original_acceptance_criteria: Acceptance checklist: calendar, booking, intake, charting, photo upload, copy, finalization/correction and payment.
original_recommended_fix: Add WebKit CI, automated accessibility checks and a short recorded acceptance script on target physical devices for launch-critical flows.
original_launch_gate: Do not describe Chromium emulation as iOS proof.

source_title: Export audit metadata omits four generated record-keeping filenames
original_evidence: The export constructs additional record-keeping CSVs, but the audit metadata’s listed files do not include all generated files. The artifact and audit event can disagree about what was produced.
original_acceptance_criteria: Test manifest, archive entries and audit payload are exactly equal.
original_recommended_fix: Generate audit file list directly from the manifest used to build the archive.
original_launch_gate: Fold into complete-export redesign.

source_title: Selected comments and documents state production/deployment facts that the source cannot prove
original_evidence: Several documents assert hosted migration maxima, deployed state or route registration. Some older migration comments still say “NOT hosted-applied,” while newer docs say all are applied; Google route-registration language conflicts with `vercel.json`.
original_acceptance_criteria: Release job fails when migration manifest/deploy config differs from generated docs.
original_recommended_fix: Maintain one generated deployment/capability register from CI/deployment/provider evidence. Mark historical comments as historical rather than authoritative.
original_launch_gate: Do not rewrite migration history merely to update comments; reconcile in current docs. --- # PART 5 — SECURITY, MULTI-TENANCY AND PRIVACY

source_title: Authenticated members can bypass audited soft deletion of treatment passes
original_evidence: `supabase/migrations/0087_clinical_rls_delete_hardening.sql:217–263` retains authenticated DELETE policies; `0114_entry_soft_delete.sql:3–25` adds an audited soft-delete triad but does not revoke DELETE. | In local Supabase, authenticate as a member, identify a visible electrolysis or laser entry, and issue a direct table DELETE instead of the UI action.

source_title: Treatment-image storage hardening can silently remain unapplied
original_evidence: `0092_treatment_images.sql` creates authenticated storage-object policies; `0093_harden_treatment_image_storage.sql` catches `insufficient_privilege`, raises a notice, and lets the migration continue. | Apply the migrations under a role that cannot alter the platform-owned storage objects, then inspect bucket privacy and policies.

source_title: No attested production source of truth
original_evidence: The ZIP has no `.git`; CI explicitly does not deploy; no Vercel/Supabase/Stripe/provider export or release manifest was supplied. | Compare a future read-only production build SHA, migration history, policy hashes, storage posture, cron registry, and provider modes with this archive.

source_title: Cross-studio platform administration is authorized by email allowlist
original_evidence: `lib/admin.ts:1–72` resolves `ADMIN_EMAILS`; comments state membership grants cross-studio access through the service-role client; `0113_admin_action_events.sql` adds an admin audit table but not a durable role model. | In local/staging, authenticate an identity whose email is in `ADMIN_EMAILS` and access `/admin`; compare with a non-allowlisted user.

source_title: Public self-service SaaS lifecycle is absent
original_evidence: No runtime `supabase.auth.signUp`, public studio-creation route, Stripe Checkout/subscription flow, plan/entitlement model, dunning, billing portal, or automated cancellation lifecycle was found; studio creation is under `/admin/studios/new`. | Start at the public site and attempt to create, fund, configure, activate, bill, cancel, and delete a studio without admin access.

source_title: Multi-location is not an implemented domain model
original_evidence: No `organizations`, `locations`, or `location_id` model was found; studio address/time zone is singular; no rooms/resources or location roles exist. | Attempt to configure two addresses with different hours, services, practitioners, time zones, taxes, and booking pages under one customer.

source_title: Broad live client-payment safety is not production-proven
original_evidence: Repository contains strong payment code and the Stripe mutation gate passed, but no read-only Stripe account/export, endpoint configuration, delivery history, live-mode event set, or reconciliation evidence was supplied. | Use approved test-mode fixtures and a controlled live studio to evidence Connect ownership, setup, charge, duplicate delivery, out-of-order event, refund, disconnection, and reconciliation.

source_title: Required scheduled-job activation is not declaratively complete
original_evidence: Three cron handlers exist, while `vercel.json` schedules only recurring-break materialization; repository notes indicate reminders may depend on an external scheduler; production activation was not supplied. | Inventory all hosted schedulers, compare route/schedule/secret/environment, then inspect last-success and duplicate-run evidence.

source_title: Reusable calendar-feed bearer credentials are readable at studio-member scope
original_evidence: `0046_practitioner_calendar_feed_token.sql` adds raw token; `0079_calendar_feed_token_hash.sql` adds a hash but retains raw column; practitioner member SELECT policies and `lib/supabase/queries.ts` broad practitioner reads expose the row. | In local Supabase as practitioner A, query visible practitioner B and inspect `calendar_feed_token`; use it against `/calendar-feed/[token]`.

source_title: Completed treatment history has no enforced finalization or amendment model
original_evidence: Sessions do not carry an enforced finalized/version state; `DoneChartingButton` is navigation/UI completion; member UPDATE policies remain for sessions and entries. | Complete a session in the UI, then directly update its earlier entries/notes through the authenticated client.

source_title: Submitted or reviewed intake responses can be overwritten directly
original_evidence: Public actions restrict changes by workflow state, but member UPDATE RLS on intake response rows does not prohibit terminal-state mutation; direct authenticated data access bypasses UI guards. | Submit an intake locally, authenticate as a studio member, and update a response value directly through Supabase.

source_title: Appointment collision constraint treats the whole studio as one resource
original_evidence: `0030_calendar_reservations.sql` exclusion constraint keys active appointment time range by `studio_id`, not practitioner/room/resource. | Create two practitioners in one studio and attempt non-conflicting appointments at the same time.

source_title: Core tenant audit evidence is user-insertable and not uniformly transaction-mandatory
original_evidence: Legacy audit tables have member INSERT policies; several actions perform a state mutation followed by a separate audit insert and tolerate/log audit failure. | Insert a plausible audit event as a member, or force the audit insert to fail after the underlying update in local/staging.

source_title: Stripe live permission is deployment-wide rather than canonical per studio
original_evidence: `lib/stripe/server.ts:44–66,119–130` gates the Stripe secret by environment/key prefix; it does not establish a database-enforced studio approval state across every mutation. | In test/staging, enable the equivalent live-mode flag and invoke payment setup/charge paths for an unapproved studio.

source_title: “Full data export” is incomplete and memory-bound
original_evidence: `app/(app)/settings/data/actions.ts` exports selected CSVs and explicitly excludes image/payment data; archive assembly is synchronous/in-memory/base64 and omits several sensitive/ledger domains. | Create a studio with intake, signed consent, photos, payments/refunds, communications, portal events, audit and soft-deleted history; compare export contents.

source_title: Tenant authorization is predominantly coarse studio-member access
original_evidence: Many policies use `is_studio_member(studio_id)`; owner checks exist for selected settings/actions, but no complete capability/role matrix or reception/support model was found. | Create owner and practitioner memberships and exercise direct table/API operations beyond each persona’s intended UI.

source_title: Clinical and intake edits lack optimistic concurrency protection
original_evidence: No consistent row `version`/ETag/compare-and-swap pattern was found for mutable clinical/intake records. | Open the same session in two clients, save conflicting changes in sequence, and inspect the lost update.

source_title: Privacy retention, deletion, correction, and offboarding are not complete operational workflows
original_evidence: Soft deletion exists in selected domains, but no complete case workflow, retention schedule, legal hold, provider purge, backup evidence, portal/job revocation, or permanent-deletion orchestration was found. | Attempt end-to-end client deletion and studio offboarding across DB, Storage, Stripe, email/SMS, scheduled jobs, tokens, audit, backups, and export.

source_title: Losing a final-slot booking race can leave client/consent side effects
original_evidence: `app/book/[slug]/actions.ts` creates/updates client and consent state before the appointment insert; the exclusion violation returns without rolling those earlier side effects back. | Submit the same final slot concurrently with new client identities and inspect client/consent rows for the rejected request.

source_title: Public booking silently assigns the active owner and offers no practitioner selection
original_evidence: `app/book/[slug]/actions.ts:759–779` queries an active owner with `maybeSingle()` and assigns that ID; no public practitioner choice was found. | Add multiple practitioners and book publicly.

source_title: Pending invitation uniqueness is global by email
original_evidence: `0007_pending_invitations.sql` defines pending uniqueness on lower(email), not studio+email; team action reports an invitation in another studio. | Invite the same email to Studio A and Studio B before acceptance.

source_title: CSV exports do not neutralize spreadsheet formulas
original_evidence: CSV escaping in `settings/data/actions.ts` quotes delimiters but does not prefix dangerous formula-leading values. | Create a client/note beginning with a formula marker, export, and open in a spreadsheet sandbox.

source_title: Client portal access events cascade away with client deletion
original_evidence: `0111_client_portal_access_events.sql` references the client with `ON DELETE CASCADE`. | Create portal events then delete the client in local DB.

source_title: Booking audit payload duplicates raw contact and free-text data
original_evidence: Booking actions write raw email/free-text context into audit JSON in addition to canonical client/appointment records. | Book with unique contact/note values and inspect appointment audit payload.

source_title: Photo archive does not implement object purge or retention lifecycle
original_evidence: Photo archive action updates `deleted_at`/`deleted_by`; no complete object lifecycle/purge job with evidence was found. | Archive a photo and inspect the storage object.

source_title: No dedicated APM/tracing and incomplete operational observability
original_evidence: No Sentry/OpenTelemetry-like dependency or current dashboard/export was found; observability relies on console logs, selected internal event/alert tables, and provider dashboards. | Induce an email/storage/Stripe/database failure in staging and trace it across request, tenant, job, provider, and user-visible state.

source_title: CI third-party actions are tag-pinned rather than immutable-SHA pinned
original_evidence: Workflow uses version tags such as `actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/setup-node@v4`, and `supabase/setup-cli@v1`. | Review `.github/workflows/ci.yml` action references.

source_title: High-risk database/browser behavior remains unexecuted in this audit
original_evidence: 4,006 assertions across 275 non-database suites passed, but 34 database suites and eight Playwright specs were not executed because required local services/browser environment were unavailable; many tests are source guards. | Run CI-equivalent local Supabase/Postgres and Playwright lanes on the reviewed SHA.

source_title: Migration files contain stale deployment-state narrative
original_evidence: Recent migration comments include production-application statements; migration files cannot update after deployment without corrupting provenance. | Compare file comments with a hosted migration history at a later date.

source_title: Structured observation-chip migration leaves legacy records inconsistent
original_evidence: `0108` adds/changes the structured representation but explicitly performs no historical backfill. | Load legacy entries and compare chip display/search with newly edited entries.

source_title: The reported 24-hour-time claim overstates implemented scope
original_evidence: `0109` explicitly limits the preference and keeps client-facing email/SMS/public booking in 12-hour presentation. | Enable 24-hour studio preference and compare authenticated calendar with confirmation/reminder SMS/email/public surfaces.

source_title: Billing, cancellation, deletion, and export copy exceeds implemented operations
original_evidence: Public/repository pages describe subscription billing/cancellation/full export/specific deletion timing while Hone subscription billing is absent, export is partial, and deletion evidence workflow is incomplete. | Trace each public promise to a code, provider, operator, and evidence-producing workflow.

source_title: Production build depends on live Google Fonts fetch
original_evidence: `npm run build` reached Next build but failed fetching Fraunces/Inter in the network-restricted environment. | Run build with outbound network disabled.

source_title: Technical SEO and answer-engine foundations are incomplete
original_evidence: Metadata/Open Graph/Twitter elements exist, but no sitemap, robots route/file, canonical strategy, or structured data was found in the repository. | Inspect generated metadata/routes and crawl the deployed site.

source_title: Custom navigation/dialog focus management is not WCAG-ready
original_evidence: Closed mobile nav uses visual hiding/`aria-hidden` while links remain mounted; custom dialogs handle Escape but no consistent focus trap, initial focus, inert background, or return focus was verified. | Keyboard through mobile nav and custom dialogs at 390–430 px; inspect focus order and screen-reader tree.

source_title: Public rate limiting fails open during configuration/provider failure
original_evidence: `lib/rate-limit/public.ts` intentionally permits requests when rate limiting is unavailable in selected paths. | Remove/interrupt Upstash configuration and exercise public actions repeatedly.

source_title: Background automation lacks durable queue, DLQ, and tenant fairness
original_evidence: Cron/claim loops and per-run caps are appropriate for pilot use, but no durable queue/backpressure/dead-letter/per-tenant scheduling system was found. | Seed work above one run’s cap, fail a provider repeatedly, and observe fairness/recovery.

source_title: OAuth can create an Auth identity without an active studio lifecycle
original_evidence: OAuth login exists; application redirects identities without active practitioner memberships to no-access; no self-service account deletion/provisioning was found. | Authenticate a new Google identity with no invitation.

source_title: Dependency audit reports moderate vulnerabilities
original_evidence: Local npm audit reported four moderate production vulnerabilities and five moderate total, with no high/critical findings at audit time. | Run the lockfile audit in the same Node/npm environment and review advisory reachability.

source_title: Support access and customer operations are founder-centric
original_evidence: Admin pages and founder-led processes exist, but no scoped support role, ticket/case linkage, approved impersonation, tenant suspension state machine, or customer-visible status workflow was found. | Attempt to resolve a tenant issue without granting cross-studio service-role access or editing the database/provider dashboard.

source_title: Session practitioner attribution can be re-pointed, including to another studio's practitioner
original_evidence: supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql:82 sessions.practitioner_id references practitioners(id) on delete restrict; 0003_allergies_and_session_fields.sql:12 performed_by_practitioner_id references practitioners(id) on delete set null. 0094_tenant_consistency_constraints.sql adds composite same-studio FKs for client_id and appointment_id ONLY — not for either practitioner column. 0160_immutable_clinical_lineage.sql pins studio_id/client_id/session_id/block_id but names NEITHER practitioner column.
original_acceptance_criteria: None exists. tests/db/immutable-clinical-lineage.db.test.ts covers only the 0160 columns.
original_recommended_fix: Independent of L18. Fix is a same-studio composite FK plus/or a 0160-style column guard; both are additive and need no application change (no call site writes these columns from a payload — verify before revoking).
